mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above 1% for three consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate tighter policy and reduce equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-tightening period (p > 0.1), or FEDFUNDS reverts below 1% within 2 months and returns turn positive.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly UNRATE falls by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single month, it indicates labor market weakening and precedes a 20-day S&P 500 forward return decline as profit expectations cool.
failure_condition: In at least 60% of UNRATE monthly drops exceeding -0.5%, the 20-day forward return is non-negative, or the effect is explained by other variables (e.g., GDP growth).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in both HOUST (household spending) and GDPC1 (goods demand) above their prior month's levels for two consecutive months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as confidence in economic expansion strengthens.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > prev_month and GDPC1 > prev_month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative despite the dual series moving up, or the effect is not statistically significant (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO index below 100 (indicating supply contraction) combined with a 2% drop in RSAFS (retail sales) in the same month triggers a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as weak demand meets limited supply.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive or indistinguishable from baseline when both contraction signals are present.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for four consecutive months, it signals accommodative policy sustaining and a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors price in rate stability.
failure_condition: Rate cuts cease and FEDFUNDS rises; 20-day forward returns turn negative within 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: A one-standard-deviation increase in monthly PAYEMS (employment) coinciding with a 0.2% drop in UNRATE predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market strengthening offsets wage growth concerns.
failure_condition: Over 60 days, returns remain flat or decline despite the labor signal, or wage growth accelerates more than employment.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both GDPC1 (goods demand) and CPIAUCSL (inflation) by at least 0.3% each suggest accelerating price and demand pressures, predicting a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as profit margins compress.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > prev_month + 0.3% and CPIAUCSL > prev_month + 0.3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or IC < 0.05 when both proxies show acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-specific regime: during a period where CPIAUCSL > 235 (high inflation) and FEDFUNDS > 4% (tightening), the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to risk-off sentiment, regardless of other signals.
regime_hint: high inflation and tight policy regime
failure_condition: During the regime, 20-day forward returns are non-negative or not statistically different from the prior regime (p > 0.1).
